metadata.title: Gino: Knife Throw: The Design Document Came Last
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.source_doc: GDD.md in this reel (v0.1, agent-drafted, unapproved)
metadata.note: godot-gdd walker film. Board excerpts are read verbatim from GDD.md by line. Gameplay is scripted-input capture of the real main scene, same build; no human playtest exists. No paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: hand it a game design document, get back a playable Godot project. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, not a transcript, because this game was rebuilt first, and its document came after.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a 2D action platformer — guide Gino home through three hostile valleys with a sword combo, three throwing knives and three hearts — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: What happened: a Unity platformer with no levels was rebuilt in Godot first.
GDD.md was written afterwards, from the evidence.

beats.narration_text: Gino: Knife Throw came before its design document. Unity left forty scripts and a pack of art, but no levels, scenes or sound. The rebuild made all three levels. The document was written last, and nothing in it is signed off.

props.text:
Gino: Knife Throw
was built from its design document.
Unity left scripts and art,
but no levels at all.
The document was written last,
and nothing in it is signed off.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant writer: text is typed on screen over the narration, so mid-beat samples legitimately show a partial page. The finished six-line text fills the safe area and holds for the last 1.5 s.

beats.narration_text: The document separates six kinds of claim: recovered from the Unity code, invented for the rebuild, built, observed, proposed, or still waiting on a person. Built: fourteen scripts and a shader. Observed: the game's playtest passes, and forty-six assertions pass in this film's three scripted takes. Human playtests: zero.

beats.narration_text: The vision is a proposal: take Gino home through three hostile valleys with a sword, three knives and three hearts. Who it's for is left open. The pillars are read off the code: read the wind-up, commit to the combo, and knives are scarce.

beats.narration_text: Here's the core loop on the real build, played by a script, not a person. A level opens with its banner. A walker comes in and the sword meets it. Gino reaches the door and presses W, and the Level Complete panel totals the run. Every step is a cut from one take, in order.

beats.narration_text: Four experience goals, all proposed, each with a test a person has to run. The captures can only hint. The script finished Rocky Outskirts in forty-three seconds with no hits. But it never discovered the four-hit combo, and it finished the last level on half a heart.

beats.narration_text: Movement changed on purpose. Unity pushed Gino with a force of fifty and about three units a second. The rebuild runs at a hundred and five pixels a second, six and a half tiles, to suit the level sizes. Coyote time and a jump buffer are new, and an early release cuts the jump.

props.title: Faster Than Unity, on Purpose
props.visualLabel: Unity source vs. the Godot rebuild
props.excerpt: - **IMPLEMENTED** (`player.gd`): run 105 px/s (6.5 tiles/s, tuned up from Unity's 3 units/s), ground acceleration 1200 and deceleration 1600 px/s², jump speed 320 px/s with gravity 900. Releasing Space early cuts the jump to 45%. 0.1 s coyote time and a 0.12 s jump buffer are AUTHORED.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 70–70

beats.narration_text: Jumping, in play. Hold Space for the full jump, three hundred and twenty pixels a second straight up, and keep running in the air. Here the script uses the long jump to land past a walker waiting below.

beats.narration_text: The combo is Unity's: J starts a slash and further presses chain up to four. Unity's trigger dealt twenty for every hit. The rebuild makes the fourth, the magic blast, worth forty, so a full combo is exactly an enemy's hundred health. That number is the rebuild's choice.

props.title: Four Hits, a Hundred Health
props.excerpt: - **IMPLEMENTED:** Attack1–3 deal 20 each; Attack4 deals 40 (AUTHORED), so a full combo defeats a 100 HP enemy. In the air J plays a jump attack (20). The combo only chains on the ground.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 74–74

beats.narration_text: In the takes, the script lands single slashes and two-hit chains: each hit knocks the walker back out of reach. So the four-hit chain and the magic blast never appear on screen. The game's own playtest is what checks them.

beats.narration_text: Knives come from Unity too: thrown straight, picked up as daggers, capped at three. The rebuild sets the numbers: four hundred and twenty pixels a second for one point three seconds, thirty damage, and the knife leaves a fraction of a second into the throw. Gino starts every new game with none.

props.title: Three Knives, Thirty Damage
props.excerpt: - **IMPLEMENTED** (`knife.gd`): 420 px/s for 1.3 s (about 546 px), 30 damage, breaks on rock or an enemy. The knife leaves 0.15 s into the throw. Gino starts with none.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 78–78

beats.narration_text: K, in play. The knife leaves Gino's hand, flies straight across the screen and hits the walker for thirty. The count under the hearts drops to zero. The sword finishes the job.

beats.narration_text: Three enemies, each with a tell. The walker bites a fifth of a second after its cone fires. The bat curls into an orb for seven tenths of a second. The plant rears up. Unity's attack dealt two, a full heart. But health and points lived in prefabs that never arrived, so the hundred health and twenty-five points are authored.

cards.text: bite 0.2 s · orb 0.7 s · rear up 0.6 s

props.excerpt: - **SOURCE:** `EnemyAttack.cs` deals `dmg = 2`, one full heart. Unity's per-prefab health values were in prefabs that were not delivered; 100 HP and 25 points per enemy are AUTHORED.

beats.narration_text: Health is Unity's six, shown as three hearts in halves. An enemy costs a full heart, a spike half a heart, and a pit the whole level. After a hit, Gino blinks for one point one seconds. Hearts as pickups are new: the sprites were in the pack, unused.

props.title: Six Halves, Three Hearts

cards.label: Rebuild
cards.text: enemy 2 · spike 1 · pit = level · 1.1 s blink

props.excerpt: - **IMPLEMENTED:** an enemy hit costs 2 (a heart), spikes 1 (half a heart). A hit gives 1.1 s of invulnerability with a blink and 0.35 s of hurt knockback. A pit or zero health loses the level; Retry restarts it with the score and knives Gino entered it with.

beats.narration_text: The biggest gap: Unity delivered no levels at all. All three are text maps in a Python tool, which checks them and simulates Gino's jumps frame by frame to prove every door and diamond is reachable. Rocky Outskirts teaches, Thorn Hollow climbs, Moonlit Depths has twelve enemies.

props.title: Three Levels Unity Never Had
props.excerpt: - Unity delivered no levels. All three are ASCII maps in `_tools/levels.py`, checked and route-simulated by that script, then written to `scripts/levels.gd` and `_tools/routes.json`.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 103–103

show.event: GodotDesignBoard: Three Levels Unity Never Had

beats.narration_text: Thorn Hollow and Moonlit Depths in the take. And here's what the map check missed: level three's rope bridge stops one tile short of the rock. A sixteen pixel hole over the spikes. The route jumps it, so the check passed. A trial run fell through.

beats.narration_text: Menus port Unity's: a pause menu, a victory panel with Next Level, a game-over panel with Retry, credits. The rebuild adds Continue, How to Play, a sound key and R to restart from a menu. That last one has a bug.

props.title: Unity Menus, Plus a Restart Key

cards.label: Rebuild
cards.text: Continue · How to Play · M · R restart

props.excerpt: - `Esc` or `P` pauses (Resume, Restart, Sound, Main Menu). R restarts from the pause or game-over menu. `M` toggles sound anywhere.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 112–112

beats.narration_text: The world is sixteen pixel tiles, auto-tiled from the pack's level sheet, light for the first two levels and dark for the cave. The art is the pack's. The sound isn't: Unity had a sound manager and no audio files, so twenty-three effects and three music loops were synthesized.

props.title: Pack Art, Synthesized Sound
props.status: AUTHORED world · art from the source folder

cards.label: World
cards.text: 16 px tiles · light and dark · 3 parallax layers

cards.label: Audio
cards.text: none in the source · 23 effects, 3 loops synthesized

props.excerpt: - **Audio:** the Unity export had a SoundManager but no audio files. 23 sound effects and three music loops (menu, level, cave) are synthesized by `_tools/make_assets.py`, using the Unity sound names.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 126–126

beats.narration_text: Under the hood, every scene is thin. A level scene is one node running one script with a level number, and everything else is built from the text map when it loads. Out of scope, by decision: more levels, difficulty settings, pathfinding for the bat.

props.title: One Node per Level
props.status: IMPLEMENTED · scope set by the rebuild
props.excerpt: - All 6 scenes are thin. Each level scene is one node running `level.gd` with a `level_id`; everything is built from the ASCII maps.
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 149–149

beats.narration_text: The risks section is candid. Nobody has played this by hand, and the Windows build has never run. The captures found two defects the game's own test missed: the bridge hole, and the restart error. And walkers waiting under drops bite Gino in mid-air. Five open questions remain for a person.

props.title: What a Person Still Has to Decide
props.excerpt: | R-01 | **Level 3's second rope bridge stops one tile short.** The `B` is at column 91, so the 7-tile span covers columns 91–97, but the pit runs from column 92 to 98. That leaves a 16 px hole at x 1568–1584 over the spike pit. The route jumps it, so `levels.py` passes, but in capture trials a Gino fighting a bat on the bridge stepped into it and died. Moving the `B` one column right closes it. |
props.source: GDD.md · Gino: Knife Throw @ cffbb01 · agent-drafted v0.1, unapproved · lines 157–157

show.event: GodotDesignBoard: What a Person Still Has to Decide

beats.narration_text: Verdict. This document organizes; it doesn't approve. The loop runs end to end on real input, from the menu through three levels to the credits, and to defeat and retry. The rebuild's own numbers are labelled. Two defects slipped past the game's own test. What's left is a person's call: the audience, the combo's damage, and whether the drops are fair.

artifactLines: Observed end to end: menu → 3 levels → credits; and pit → game over → retry.
Checks: the game's playtest passes · 46 film-capture assertions pass.
Found: a 16 px hole in level 3's bridge; R on a menu logs a script error.
Pending a person: audience, combo damage, drops, 0 playtests.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with your own design document: Here is my game's design document. Pick one proposed experience goal. Rewrite it as a hypothesis with a test I can run with three players, and tell me which result would make me change the design. If no result would change your mind, it isn't a hypothesis yet. Liam, in for Bear.
